title: The 10 Best Cordless Detail Sanders
subtitle: Battery-powered mouse and detail sanders for corners, trim and furniture, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A cordless detail sander has the same pointed, iron-shaped pad as a corded mouse sander, so it reaches into corners and along trim where a round pad can't, but there's no cord to drag over the finish. We ranked 10 current best-sellers on rating, review volume and features: brushless motor, variable speed, a shop-vac port, and whether a battery and charger come in the box. Most run at about 12,000 orbits per minute, so the bigger choices are battery platform and kit versus bare tool. Prices run from $40.84 for the GALAX PRO kit to $92.74 for the WORX WX822L kit.

avoid.name: DEKOPRO Cordless Multi-Function Mouse Detail Sander with 3 Attachments and 12 Sandpapers
avoid.flag: Listing contradicts itself on what's in the box
avoid.verdict: You can't tell from the listing whether it can run when it arrives. The package list includes a charger but no battery, while the product details list a battery pack but no charger.
reasons: The "What You Would Get" bullet lists the sander, 3 attachments, 12 sandpapers, a dust collector, a manual and a charger, with no battery. The "Included Components" field lists a battery pack and no charger. One of them is wrong.
It only says "20V lithium ion" and never names a battery platform or capacity, so if a part is missing you don't know what to buy.
It calls its dust collector a "built-in vacuum attachment" but never gives a hose size, unlike the CRAFTSMAN CMCW221B, which states 1-1/4 inch.
For $2.85 more, the GALAX PRO kit clearly lists a 1.3Ah battery, a charger and 20 sandpapers.

buyers_guide.q: What's the difference between a detail sander and a random orbital sander?
buyers_guide.a: A detail (mouse) sander has a pointed, iron-shaped pad that reaches into corners and along trim. A random orbital sander has a round 5-inch pad that removes material faster on flat surfaces but can't get into a 90-degree corner. Many people own both.

buyers_guide.q: Should I buy a kit or a bare tool?
buyers_guide.a: If you already own batteries for BLACK+DECKER, CRAFTSMAN, WORX or DeWalt, buy the bare tool and use what you have. If you don't, a kit is cheaper than buying the tool, battery and charger separately. On this page, the BLACK+DECKER kit is only $5 more than its bare tool.

buyers_guide.q: Is there a DeWalt, Milwaukee or Makita cordless mouse sander?
buyers_guide.a: DeWalt doesn't sell a mouse sander. Milwaukee's M12 FUEL orbital detail sander exists, but Amazon had no seller for it when we checked. For DeWalt 20V batteries, third-party tools like the Mellif and TRONYAN on this page fill the gap. They aren't made or backed by DeWalt.

buyers_guide.q: Does battery size matter on a detail sander?
buyers_guide.a: It sets runtime. A 1.3Ah or 1.5Ah pack is fine for a few doors or a chair; a 2.0Ah pack lasts longer between charges. If you plan to sand a whole room of trim, get a spare battery or a kit with a 2.0Ah pack.

buyers_guide.q: Do I need a vacuum port?
buyers_guide.a: For small jobs the dust bag is enough. For long sessions indoors, a shop-vac connection pulls far more dust off the work. On this page only the CRAFTSMAN CMCW221B lists a 1-1/4-inch vacuum connection.
